newsitem.title: USA: U.S. REVIEWING DUTCH SWINE FEVER OUTBREAKS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. REVIEWING DUTCH SWINE FEVER OUTBREAKS.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) is looking into a recent outbreak of swine fever in the Netherlands and it is too early to say if any restrictions might be set on imports, an APHIS spokeswoman said Wednesday.
"We're in the reviewing and information gathering stages," said the spokeswoman, who asked not to be identified.
The U.S. imports swine and swine products from the Netherlands, which has a hog cholera-free status.
The Dutch goverment said Tuesday it had discovered an outbreak of swine fever in the south of the country and as a precaution had closed off the one farm involved and two nearby slaughterhouses.
